traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements from 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX are implemented and verified:
1) File-Level Template: Implemented by ensureFileSupportsAnnotation + insertSupportsTemplate + buildSupportsTemplateComment. When a test file lacks any @supports comment and autoFixTestTemplate is true, the rule reports missingFileSupports with a fixer that inserts a file-top JSDoc block containing a generic @supports line and a TODO. This matches the story’s template example and is covered by the [REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE] test case.
2) Format Fixes for [REQ-XXX] prefixes: Implemented by normalizeReqId + normalizeReqPrefixInDescription and used from handleItOrTestCall when autoFixTestPrefixFormat is enabled. The helpers normalize: - Extra spaces: "[ REQ-TEST-FIX ]" → "[REQ-TEST-FIX]". - Underscores: "[REQ_TEST_FIX]" → "[REQ-TEST-FIX]". - Lowercase: "[req-lowercase]" → "[REQ-LOWERCASE]". - Parentheses: "(REQ-PAREN)" → "[REQ-PAREN]". All these cases have explicit RuleTester fixtures with code and expected output that currently pass.
3) Template Quality: The default template uses clear placeholders (`docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ`) plus an explicit TODO sentence telling developers to replace them with real values. That directly satisfies the requirement for clear placeholders and no inference of real paths or IDs.
4) Quality & Safety: Auto-fixes are restricted to: - Inserting a comment block at a safe lexical position (top of file or after shebang) without touching executable code. - Rewriting only the string literal test name while preserving quoting and escaping, with changes limited to first-argument descriptions containing an obvious REQ identifier at the start. If a canonical `[REQ-...]` prefix is already present, no change is made. If there is no recognizable REQ at the start (e.g., `"missing prefix"`), only an error is reported and no fix is provided. This aligns with REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
5) Integration with ESLint --fix and existing validation rules: The rule is an ESLint RuleModule with meta.fixable: "code" and is exercised via RuleTester with `output` expectations, which is exactly how ESLint’s --fix behavior is modeled. It composes with existing validation (from Story 020.0) in a single rule: the same rule both validates and, when run with --fix, performs these safe auto-fixes.
6) User Experience: Templates are consistent (single default pattern with TODO guidance) and applied uniformly across test files; prefix normalization always results in the canonical `[REQ-...]` format. Test cases show straightforward, predictable before/after transformations.
7) Error Handling: Fixers are only attached when conditions are clearly safe (e.g., autoFix options enabled, recognizable REQ pattern, literal string argument). Otherwise, the rule reports messages without attempting to change code, as required.
8) Documentation: The user-docs/api-reference.md section for traceability/require-test-traceability documents the auto-fix behavior and configuration options corresponding to this story. Combined with the README reference, this satisfies the story’s documentation criterion.
Given the concrete implementation in the rule and helpers, the passing targeted tests, and the documented behavior, this story is fully implemented and passes all acceptance criteria.
